title: Sebastian and the Debt
premise: Edmund Thornbury, a disgraced intelligence analyst with three agencies' worth of enemies and one packed go-bag, is approached by a stranger named Sebastian who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of doing. The debt is real to him, and he intends to repay it by pulling her into a conspiracy surrounding an upcoming economic summit, where a mole plans to trade a secret worth killing for. As Sebastian's protection becomes obsession and her old handlers circle back, Edmund discovers the favor never happened: Sebastian manufactured the debt to recruit the only analyst who ever spotted the mole's pattern. To survive the summit, Edmund must decide whether to burn the secret, sell it, or trust the found family she never meant to build — ending with her exposing the mole at the summit while choosing to stay, unpacking the go-bag at last.
about_author: Emrys Sterling is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade adjacent to the world of briefings, burn notices, and quiet betrayals before turning to fiction. Sterling writes thrillers about people whose loyalties are tested in rooms where nothing is written down.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Three months after her third firing, Edmund lives out of a packed duffel in a rented room, polishing the lie that she 'left voluntarily.' A routine errand turns wrong when she spots surveillance she recognizes from her old life. Emotional beat: paranoia as habit, loneliness disguised as preparedness.

chapters.title: A Favor Returned
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A calm stranger, Sebastian, intercepts her at a laundromat and repays a debt — money, documents, a warning — for saving his life in Sarajevo, an event Edmund cannot recall. He leaves a card with no name. Emotional beat: uncanny gratitude from a stranger who knows too much.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian watches Edmund from across the street, rehearsing the story he built for her, guilt flickering under conviction. His handler texts a deadline. He tells himself the debt is real enough. Emotional beat: a good man lying to himself.

chapters.title: The Old Pattern
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Bored, Edmund runs the summit delegate list through an old analytical habit and finds a funding anomaly no one else flagged — the same signature she spotted years ago and was disbelieved. Someone tries her door lock at 3 a.m. Emotional beat: the analyst waking up inside her.

chapters.title: Recruited by Debt
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Sebastian reappears, offering protection and resources if she helps him trace the anomaly before the summit. She refuses; hours later her room is tossed and her go-bag stolen. With nowhere left to run, she calls his number. Emotional beat: cornered consent.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In a cramped safehouse, Sebastian lays down rules; Edmund breaks all of them by morning, reading his files and finding gaps in his Sarajevo story. Their friction sparks something like respect. Emotional beat: two guarded people negotiating proximity.

chapters.title: What the Files Say
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian reports to his handler, Voss, who pushes him to accelerate recruitment of 'the analyst.' We learn Sebastian fabricated the Sarajevo debt on Voss's orders but has begun believing his own cover. Emotional beat: complicity curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, One Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund contacts a former colleague, Priya, who confirms someone has been quietly erasing Edmund's old findings from archives. The mole isn't just active — it's been cleaning house around her for years. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by terror.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A surveillance team follows Edmund to a dead drop; Sebastian extracts her through a market in a tense chase. He takes a knife graze shielding her. Emotional beat: the first unguarded moment — fear metabolized into trust.

chapters.title: Stitches and Secrets
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. While Edmund stitches his arm, she asks what really happened in Sarajevo. He gives her half the truth. Later, alone, he drafts a resignation message to Voss and deletes it. Emotional beat: love beginning where the lie should have ended.

chapters.title: Priya's Price
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Priya agrees to pull archived originals but wants Edmund's silence about her own compromises. Edmund realizes everyone in this world owes someone. The archive request trips an alarm somewhere. Emotional beat: loyalty as currency, spent carefully.

chapters.title: The Mole's Face
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Cross-referencing the anomaly, Edmund identifies Deputy Summit Coordinator Alaric Vane — the man who once signed off on dismissing her findings. That night, Vane's people find Priya. Emotional beat: triumph immediately punished.

chapters.title: Ashes of an Ally
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Priya survives an 'accident,' barely, and Edmund understands the cost of involving anyone. She tries to push Sebastian away to protect him; he refuses to leave. Emotional beat: found family forming against her will.

chapters.title: Voss Unmasked
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian confronts Voss, demanding they stand down now that Vane is identified. Voss reveals the operation's true aim: not stopping Vane, but controlling what he sells. Sebastian realizes he was bait all along. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that made him.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian tells Edmund the truth: there was no Sarajevo favor; the debt was invented to recruit her. He expects her to walk. Instead she says the work matters more than the lie — but the trust will have to be rebuilt. Emotional beat: devastation, then a harder, realer bond.

chapters.title: What Vane Sells
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Decoding intercepted material, Edmund learns Vane's secret: proof that a summit member state engineered the crisis the summit exists to solve — leverage worth billions and countless lives. Whoever holds it owns the peace. Emotional beat: the weight of the one secret worth killing for.

chapters.title: Every Exit Closed
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Vane's cleaners, Voss's operators, and Edmund's old agency all converge on the safehouse. The trio scatters per protocol; Sebastian is taken. Edmund faces the go-bag choice: flee abroad or go back for him. Emotional beat: duty versus love, finally forced to pick.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund offers Vane's own intermediaries a deal: Sebastian's location for access to the summit's security floor, trading the one thing she swore she'd never give up — her anonymity, her last protection. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Held in a black site, Sebastian stalls his interrogators using everything Edmund taught him about misdirection. He learns Voss intends to let Vane complete the sale and take credit. Emotional beat: faith in someone else as survival tactic.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Minutes
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Inside the summit perimeter with forged credentials, Edmund has minutes to expose Vane before the signing ceremony. She triggers the building's document system to broadcast the evidence to every delegation simultaneously. Vane moves to stop her personally. Emotional beat: the analyst's quiet skills weaponized at last.

chapters.title: The Room Where It Ends
chapters.summary: POV Edmund and Sebastian alternating. Confrontation in the service corridors: Vane falls, Voss's operation collapses when delegations demand investigations, and Sebastian arrives wounded but walking to stand between Edmund and the last gun. Emotional beat: climax — love proven in action, not words.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Weeks later, testimony given, names cleared partially, Edmund signs onto a small independent oversight unit with Sebastian and a recovering Priya. She unpacks the go-bag, item by item, keeping only the first-aid kit. Emotional beat: belonging chosen deliberately; the debt repaid by staying.
